core: the strict causal future {x | ∃ z ∈ Σ, z ≤ x, x ≠ z} and strict past of Σ are open. Sufficient: (chronal form) C.PushUp and every point in Z^+ and Z^-; or (two-sided form) IsLocallyCauchyTwoSided plus J^±_⊤(V) open for every open V; or (gx form) PushUp + Z^+ = M for the past side and two-sidedness + J^+_⊤(V) open for the future side

findings: SETTLED under CurvesExtend + PushUp + Z^± = M, NOT as stated: the bare DEC-44 form (isCauchySurface_of_isLocallyCauchy) holds, with no splitting and no two-sidedness, as soon as curves extend, C has push-up and every point is strongly tarentin in the past and the future (isCauchySurface_of_isLocallyCauchy_of_chronal). None of these three is a hypothesis of the bare form. On every static spacetime ℝ × X over a proper connected geodesic space it holds with exactly the bare hypotheses (staticCausality.isCauchySurface_of_compact_isLocallyCauchy); Minkowski space is an instance (checked), ℝ × flat torus is one mathematically but no torus instance is built in the library. This is what Barbot's Rem 2.3 (l.576-578) and §11 (l.3537-3540, 3578-3580) need, for regular flat spacetimes.

The splitting is not what the proof needs: it is sufficient that the strict causal future and past of Σ be open (necessity is not shown). Acausality then follows from connectedness of Σ alone (the strictly related part of Σ is open by hypothesis, closed because the relation of a GH spacetime is closed and Σ is locally acausal near the diagonal, and misses a ≤-minimal point of Σ found by Zorn on the compact diamonds Σ ∩ J^-(w)); J^+(Σ) ∪ J^-(Σ) is then clopen, hence M. Under that openness hypothesis a 'fold' of Σ (meeting a line twice, winding twice round a cylinder) is excluded by the connectedness step, with no projection.

For gx (BTZ): the bare form is NOT settled. At a BTZ point Z^- fails (SingularFlatAxioms.mem_Zminus_iff) and J^+(Σ)\Σ ≠ I^+(Σ), so only the past side comes for free (push-up and Z^+ = M are fields of SingularFlatAxioms). Sufficient for gx: CurvesExtend (not a field of SingularFlatAxioms; every form here carries it) plus openness of the strict causal future of Σ; the latter follows from two-sidedness in the charts plus 'J^+_⊤(V) open for V open' (isCauchySurface_of_isLocallyCauchyTwoSided_of_pushUp).

No counterexample to the bare form was found. By the chronal form, a counterexample must break at least one of CurvesExtend, PushUp, Z^+ = M, Z^- = M (e.g. BTZ-like points, where Z^- fails), and so cannot be a static spacetime over a proper connected geodesic space.
questions: Is J^+_⊤(V) open for every open V in a singular flat spacetime (E_{≥0}-manifold) - i.e. is it future causally open at BTZ lines? If yes (a model fact), the bare form of Lemma K holds for gx through isCauchySurface_of_isLocallyCauchyTwoSided_of_pushUp, given two-sidedness in the charts.

kb_proposals: Lemma K does not need a splitting: it needs the strict causal future/past of Σ open; acausality is then a clopen argument on Σ (Zorn on Σ ∩ J^-(w) for a minimal point), see LemmaKBare.
CurvesExtend.dual now exists (LemmaKBare); together with Inextensible.dual_reverse it lets every curve-extension argument be dualised.
